result.title: Training Autoregressive Language Models on Rounded, Bounded, and Censored Numerical Labels via Exact Likelihood
result.summary: Numerical labels often specify a set of possible values: a measurement is rounded, a laboratory test reports only a bound, or a program is stopped at a timeout. We introduce boundary marginalization, the first method that trains an autoregressive language model on the exact likelihood of such observations through its existing digit tokens. A fixed-width, order-preserving numeral representation groups consecutive grid values under shared digit prefixes. An interval is a union of such groups, so its exact probability and gradient follow from at most two boundary paths, the successive digit prefixes of its endpoints, each of length logarithmic in the number of grid values. The resulting objective unifies precise, rounded, bounded, and censored supervision and trains digit decisions at the resolution supplied by each observation. The same computation supports exact distributional queries and unbiased gradients for the continuous ranked probability score on exact labels. Experiments show recovery of a conditional distribution from rounded and censored reports alone, improved likelihood on naturally censored molecular measurements, and more accurate code latency distributions on two backbones. Exact interval updates remain tractable as the numerical support grows to one million values.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 boundary marginalization：在定宽、保序的数字表示下，用至多两条边界前缀路径精确计算区间的似然与梯度，从而用同一目标训练自回归模型处理精确、四舍五入、有上下界和删失（如超时）的数值标签。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基于数字 token 前缀的区间似然与删失监督，可能可供核查是否用于离散化 latent 状态或截断观测（如预算耗尽即停止）的精确概率训练；但该工作针对纯文本数值输出标签，与 VLM 推理内部状态无直接关联。
